Alex (sales): BigBank POC stuck - Windows desktops behind corp proxy. Python SDK streaming never starts, client logs show CONNECT then 407. Anyone seen WinHTTP/PAC/NTLM quirks?
Jamie (SE): Can you paste the SDK logs? root stack + request headers (no secrets). Also which proxy flow are they using (PAC/explicit/NTLM)?
Alex (sales): Snippet from the agent: 
```
2026-03-19 15:03:12 INFO request sent: method=POST url=https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
2026-03-19 15:03:12 DEBUG proxy response: 407 Proxy Authentication Required
```
Cory (support): 407 + corporate PAC = classic headache. Windows machines often use WinHTTP/WinINet which doesn't always respect HTTP_PROXY env vars. Our SDK (requests/urllib3) reads envs, but system PAC + NTLM handshakes are different. Try local CNTLM or import system proxy to winhttp.
Irina (eng): Also: streaming over an NTLM gateway can break because NTLM ties auth to the TCP connection. If the SDK reuses connections or does HTTP/1.1 pipelining the auth fails. Workarounds: disable connection pooling or force `Connection: close` for the streaming request.
Jamie (SE): Quick repro checklist I use:
1) `netsh winhttp show proxy` to see winhttp config
2) `netsh winhttp import proxy source=ie` to copy IE/Edge settings into winhttp
3) or run CNTLM locally and set `HTTPS_PROXY=http://localhost:3128`
4) test with curl: `curl -v --proxy http://localhost:3128 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health`
Alex (sales): We tried CNTLM earlier - curl via localhost worked, but SDK still returns 407. They may be using NTLMv2 + negotiate.
Cory (support): If CNTLM forwards but SDK doesn't authenticate, you can either: (a) perform NTLM auth in-app (requests-ntlm) or (b) run an NTLM-aware system proxy that terminates auth. Example for Python: 
```
from requests_ntlm import HttpNtlmAuth
session.auth = HttpNtlmAuth('DOMAIN\\\\user','password')
```
That will do NTLM within the HTTP client instead of relying on system.
Irina (eng): For streaming specifically, try this quick tweak in the SDK (temporary patch): set `session.headers['Connection'] = 'close'` and disable `PoolManager` reuse for the streaming call. I'll open a small debug branch with a `disable_connection_pooling` flag.
Jamie (SE): Another gotcha - PAC files sometimes return different proxy hosts for different domains. Confirm the PAC resolution for `api.redwood.ai` (use `pactester` or browser devtools). Also check if the corp gateway does TLS interception; if so you need to add the MITM CA to the SDK's CA bundle or Windows trust store.
Alex (sales): Copying the IT contact at BigBank to ask about TLS MITM and PAC. Will also ask them to run `netsh winhttp show proxy` and send the output.
deploy-bot: CI canary: sdk-windows-proxy integration test failed on 2026-03-19 build 7892 - failing test `streaming_through_ntlm`.
Alex (sales): Update from BigBank: `netsh winhttp show proxy` returned an explicit proxy and auth method = NTLM. They ran CNTLM -> curl worked. Attaching verbose SDK log (redacted).
Jamie (SE): Thanks. If curl via CNTLM works but SDK still 407, confirm the SDK process inherits the HTTPS_PROXY env var in the service environment (systemd/windows service env won't always include user envs).
Cory (support): Also validate Windows service user: if the app runs as SYSTEM it won't have user credentials for NTLM. CNTLM running as the service user or using machine credentials is needed.
Irina (eng): We're going to push a short-lived debug build that adds `--proxy-mode=system|env|direct` and `--disable-keepalive-for-proxy` flags so you can test without code changes. Jamie and I can pair on a remote session.
Alex (sales): Perfect - I'll schedule a screen share with BigBank and include you both. Thanks all :pray: 
Jamie (SE): Good plan. If needed we'll recommend the customer use a short-lived dedicated NAT/proxy in their DMZ for the POC to avoid NTLM entanglement.
Cory (support): Filed internal follow-up ticket for docs: "Windows proxy: CNTLM + SDK notes" and a troubleshooting checklist.
Alex (sales): Screen share scheduled for tomorrow 10:00 PDT. I'll paste logs in this thread afterwards.
